sections.heading: Choosing a drying speed
sections.body: The faster a glue dries, the less time you have to place and adjust each lash, so very fast glues suit experienced volume artists and slower glues suit beginners and classic work. Humidity changes drying speed too: lash glue sets faster in humid air and slower in dry air, which is why many artists in Nairobi keep two glues for the dry and rainy seasons.

sections.heading: Storing your glue

Unopened glue keeps about a year; once opened, use it within 1-3 months for the best bond.

sections.heading: What classic lashes are for

Classic lashes are the base of every lash menu: one extension on one natural lash. They give a mascara look that suits first-time clients, office looks and anyone who wants definition rather than volume.

The 0.15mm thickness is the usual starting point. Go down to 0.10mm or 0.12mm for fine or weak natural lashes, and use 0.18mm or 0.20mm only on strong, healthy lashes.

Unopened glue keeps about a year; once opened, use it within 1-3 months for the best bond.

sections.heading: Why L curls
sections.body: Many clients have straight or downward-growing natural lashes, or hooded and monolid eyes where a C or D curl disappears under the lid. The flat base of an L curl bonds along more of the natural lash and then turns up, so the set stays visible and lifts the eye.

sections.heading: L, L+, LC or LD?
sections.body: L has the straightest base and a sharp lift. L+ lifts a little more. LC and LD have a softer, rounder L shape that blends with C and D curl sets, so they are useful on the inner and outer corners.

sections.heading: Application tips

sections.heading: Choosing a drying speed

Take it out about 20 minutes before use so it reaches room temperature, shake well, and wipe the nozzle clean before closing. Unopened glue keeps about a year; once opened, use it within 1-3 months for the best bond.

sections.heading: Isolation or volume tweezers?
sections.body: Isolation tweezers are long and straight or gently curved; you use them in your non-working hand to separate one natural lash.
